newsitem.title: CHINA: China says ex-official being held in good care.
newsitem.headline: China says ex-official being held in good care.

text.p: China said on Monday a former senior Chinese official who vanished into effective house arrest after completing a jail term last May was waiting for new housing and was in good care.

Bao Tong, 63, was freed from prison last May after serving a seven-year sentence for his role in the 1989 pro-democracy protests in China, but has since been held at a dormitory of the State Council, or cabinet, near Beijing.

"High-level departments think he is not suitable any more for ministerial-level housing and want to change his residence but have so far failed to do so," said Zhang Xiufu, executive vice-minister of justice when asked about Bao's whereabouts.

Bao held ministerial status when he was secretary to the Communist Party's powerful Politburo in the late 1980s. He was the most senior official to be jailed after the 1989 pro-democracy demonstrations.
"Because a two-year suspension of his political rights still applies to Bao Tong, so some administrative bodies are exercising management measures," Zhang told a news conference.
Bao's case has drawn fire from the United States, which has protested against his detention without recourse to judicial representation and without access to his family.
Zhang defended Bao's detention, saying Beijing's measures were necessary and required by law.
"The relevant departments are taking good care of him," he said.

Bao, once an aide to former Communist Party chief Zhao Ziyang who was sacked after the 1989 student-led demonstrations, was convicted of "counter-revolutionary incitement" and the leaking of state secrets.

Diplomats in Beijing say Bao is a source of anxiety for China's leaders, who fear he may reveal details of the dealings of the highest party echelons in the weeks before the bloody 1989 crackdown on demonstrators.
